snapshot.central_hypothesis: Under controlled hyperosmotic perturbation, membrane-bounded organelles resist internal densification and maintain sharp lipid-defined boundaries, whereas fluid-like phase-separated condensates undergo continuous density shifts and boundary coarsening; this distinction holds provided that global cytoskeletal integrity is maintained and non-specific macromolecular precipitation is excluded.
snapshot.claim_scope: Nanoscale biomolecular organization in crowded cellular environments, specifically proposing a design-only computational strategy to distinguish membrane-bounded organelles from fluid-like phase-separated condensates via modeled osmotic and macromolecular crowding gradients, bounded by conditions where global cytoskeletal collapse and non-specific salting-out are controlled.
snapshot.mechanism_or_relation: Osmotic pressure gradients modulate macromolecular crowding and multivalent interactions to drive dispersed-to-aggregated transitions in phase-separated condensates, while lipid bilayer impermeability restricts membrane-bounded organelles to volume reduction without internal densification.
snapshot.title: Osmotic and Macromolecular Crowding Gradients Discriminate Membrane-Bounded from Phase-Separated Compartmentalization via Cryo-Electron Tomography

assumptions: Cryo-ET can resolve nanoscale spatial density profiles without fixation artifacts; aquaporin inhibition specifically blocks water flux; hyperosmotic conditions can be applied without inducing global cytoskeletal collapse or non-specific protein precipitation.
hypothesis.boundary_or_failure_condition: The claim fails if membrane-bounded organelles exhibit continuous density gradients and fusion due to cytoskeletal compression, or if phase-separated condensates maintain sharp boundaries, or if non-specific salting-out produces identical density profiles across all compartments.
hypothesis.central_hypothesis: Under controlled hyperosmotic perturbation, membrane-bounded organelles resist internal densification and maintain sharp lipid-defined boundaries, whereas fluid-like phase-separated condensates undergo continuous density shifts and boundary coarsening; this distinction holds provided that global cytoskeletal integrity is maintained and non-specific macromolecular precipitation is excluded.
hypothesis.claim_scope: Nanoscale biomolecular organization in crowded cellular environments, specifically proposing a design-only computational strategy to distinguish membrane-bounded organelles from fluid-like phase-separated condensates via modeled osmotic and macromolecular crowding gradients, bounded by conditions where global cytoskeletal collapse and non-specific salting-out are controlled.
hypothesis.discriminating_observation: Differential boundary sharpness and internal spatial density profiles measured via cryo_tomography_assay: condensates exhibit continuous density gradients and fusion, while membrane-bounded organelles exhibit sharp density discontinuities and volume reduction without fusion, under conditions where cytoskeletal artifacts are controlled.
hypothesis.evidence_basis: Computational synthesis of cryo-fluorescence microscopy and cryo-electron tomography measurements of spatial density profiles under osmotic gradients, supplemented by design-only experimental proposals marked NEED_HUMAN_INPUT.
hypothesis.evidence_requirement: Computational synthesis and proposed measurement of spatial density profiles and boundary sharpness differentials between membrane-bounded and phase-separated compartments under osmotic gradients, contrasted against water-flux ablation and swelling stress boundaries, with explicit controls for cytoskeletal and salting-out artifacts.
hypothesis.expected_mechanism: Hyperosmotic shock increases macromolecular crowding, driving phase-separated condensates to densify or undergo Ostwald ripening via steric exclusion, while membrane-bounded organelles shrink but maintain sharp boundaries; this mechanism is contingent on the absence of global cytoskeletal collapse.
hypothesis.intervention_or_transformation: Computational modeling and proposed design-only biological perturbation of osmotic_crowding_gradients (hyperosmotic shock) and aquaporin_inhibition_ablation, marked NEED_HUMAN_INPUT for feasibility and ethics review.
hypothesis.mechanism_or_relation: Osmotic pressure gradients modulate macromolecular crowding and multivalent interactions to drive dispersed-to-aggregated transitions in phase-separated condensates, while lipid bilayer impermeability restricts membrane-bounded organelles to volume reduction without internal densification.
